newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times business - Dec 4.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times business - Dec 4.

text.p: The New York Times reported the following business stories on Wednesday:
- Delta Air Lines and Continental Airlines are holding talks about a possible merger.
The McDonnell Douglas Corp and the Boeing Co said they reached a cooperative agreement to collaborate on the development of wide-body aircraft.
- Three former officers of Archer Daniels Midland Co were indicted by a federal grand jury on charges that they conspired with competitors to fix the prices of feed additive.
- The index of leading economic indicators rose by one-tenth of one percent in October.

- IBM entered the debt markets by offering an issue of 100-year bonds that yield 7.22 percent. - Advanta, the credit card issuer, temporarily agreed to stop marketing the Rewards Accelerator credit card, following legal attacks from other credit card issuers.
- Lucas Varity, the London-based auto parts company, said it would sell 13 businesses, take a charge of $420 million and cut 3,000 jobs as part of a two-year streamlining.
- Prudential Insurance policy holders requested that a Federal judge step down from presiding over a dispute between the insurer and policyholders, saying the judge held a private meeting
- Analysts say the going could be bumpy for TCI Satellite Entertainment, which begins trading Wednesday.
- General Motors reported dismal auto sales for the second consecutive month.
- Japan's economy showed unexpected signs of resumed growth in the third quarter.
- A.C. Nielsen agreed with the European Commission to end pricing practices that Information Resources said had thwarted competition in sales tracking services.
- The Dow Jones industrial average tumbled late Tuesday as the General Motors Corp reported poor auto sales for November.
